title: A conference, a castle, and a very convenient pool.
summary: A Gaylord Palms Fiber Connect conference, Disney’s Pop Century stay, a Skyliner ride and a Crystal Palace meal—with original photos and practical Orlando travel notes.
search: The journal/Travel · Orlando, Florida Fiber Connect, with the Graphical Networks team.A working trip, with a little room for wonderA conference, a castle, and a very convenient pool.Fiber Connect brought me to Florida. Staying at Disney gave the hours around work a little extra charm.Published October 6, 2026 Work: Fiber ConnectStay: Pop CenturyFlight: JetBlueMap & placesPractical tipsPrint a planning list There are work trips where the hotel is simply where you leave your suitcase. On this one, I stayed at Disney’s Pop Century Resort—and the pool was right outside my room.An excellent detail. Possibly the detail I should lead with.I flew JetBlue to Florida for Fiber Connect with Graphical Networks. The conference took place at the beautiful Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center, while Pop Century was my home base. Around the work came a lovely Skyliner ride, the Crystal Palace buffet, and a little time at Disney.I’m a longtime fan of Funspot in New Hampshire and the documentary The King of Kong: A Fistful of Quarters.Michael and James stayed home. The Evil Queen, however, made an appearance. ;) A little Magic Kingdom time around the work schedule.A Disney address for a working tripThe pleasure of being close.Gaylord Palms was a lovely setting for the conference. Staying at Pop Century gave the trip another atmosphere altogether: bright, playful, and unmistakably Disney.And then there was that pool. Having it right outside my room was such a pleasure. After a day of work, I appreciated being close to something enjoyable without having to organize another outing.Even when James isn’t traveling with me, I notice those practical details. How far is the walk? How easily could we return to the room? Is the thing we would most enjoy conveniently nearby?Those questions matter just as much to me as a hotel’s photographs. The journey gets a place in the storyThe Skyliner was part of the pleasure.I loved the Skyliner ride. Transportation can feel like something to get through, but this was a lovely part of the trip itself.Pop Century is connected through the Skyliner network to EPCOT and Disney’s Hollywood Studios. It is worth looking at the route and current operating information before building the day around it.My own takeaway was simpler: leave time to enjoy the ride.Official Skyliner routes and operating updates →Original editorial illustration. The bright dining room, the buffet, and a visit from Eeyore made a memorable combination.I still found myself thinking about how the experience might work for our family. Being able to see food before choosing it can be useful. So can knowing beforehand that characters may approach the table.For a future visit with James, I would look at the current food choices, preview the setting, and plan around what felt comfortable for him. This was my trip, so those are considerations for another visit—not things I tested with him.Crystal Palace is inside Magic Kingdom. title: Before you go.
summary: Practical notes to copy and adapt before an outing, school meeting or everyday plan. Clear questions, useful wording and details worth checking.
search: The original practical notesBefore you go.The questions to ask. The words to borrow.Open just the note you need. Copy it, edit it for your situation and keep personal information limited to what is useful. The practical detailsQuestions to ask and notes to borrow. Open whatever you need. Plan a day out Seven questions before you go A little more information before leaving the house can save a lot of guessing when you get there. When is it quieter?Ask about crowds, music, hand dryers, and scheduled events. Where can we take a break?Check for a calm space and whether you can leave and re-enter. What are the bathrooms like?Ask about privacy, space, and the specific facilities you need. What can we bring?Confirm food, drinks, communication devices, and familiar comfort items. How does the visit actually work?Check queues, parking distance, steps, seating, and any required waiting. Is the main attraction open?Confirm today's availability, hours, age rules, and access restrictions. What happens if plans change?Ask about cancellation, refunds, and a shorter visit before booking. ShareCopyPrint Ask for access A clear request can be short. Explain what gets in the way, say what would help, and ask for a reply in writing. A note you can borrow Hi, we're planning to visit [place] on [date]. A family member has a disability, and [barrier] makes it difficult to take part. Would it be possible to [specific adjustment]? Please let us know what you can arrange and who to ask for when we arrive. If that won't work, is there another option? A written reply would help us plan. Thank you! Copy this request Be specificCould we wait somewhere quieter until it's our turn?Could you send a few photos or tell us what happens during the visit?Can our support person stay with us?Could we have the instructions in writing too? You can begin with the access need. Your family's entire history needn't go into the first email. US guidance: businesses open to the public and effective communication. Duties and exceptions depend on the setting. This is a starting point for a request, not individual legal advice. Hotels and pools A lovely lobby is a bonus. A working pool and the right beds are rather more important. The room: what are the actual beds? Does the separate sleeping area have a door? “Suite” leaves a surprising amount unanswered.The pool: is it open on your dates? And the hot tub? Ask about hours, age rules, and water temperature if it matters to you.The timing: can you swim before check-in or after checkout?The food: what exactly is in the kitchenette? A fridge and microwave won't do the same job as a stove.The noise: ask about events, room location, and somewhere to take a quiet break.The bill: get the total with taxes, parking, fees, and deposits. Read the cancellation terms before paying. Hi, we're looking at a stay on [dates]. Could you confirm the beds and room layout, what's in the kitchenette, and whether both the indoor pool and hot tub will be open? We'd also like their hours and age rules, and whether we can use them before check-in or after checkout. Please include the total with mandatory fees, any deposit, and the cancellation terms. We also need [access adjustment]. Thanks so much! Copy the hotel questions Ask the property about your actual dates. An old pool photograph can only tell you so much. Support communication Please speak to the person. Give them time to answer. Those two things are a very good place to start. AAC means augmentative and alternative communication. Speech, vocalizations, gestures, signs, photographs, objects, writing, spelling, eye gaze, switches, low-tech boards and speech-generating devices can all be part of one multimodal system. Keep the person's communication method within reach. Understand ableism Ableism can show up in an ordinary exchange: talking over someone, dismissing an access request, or assuming a person won't enjoy an activity because they need help with it. Some autistic people need substantial support throughout their lives. They still have preferences, privacy, and every reason to be included.
